summary: The current Slate Point lookout is the third structure on the site, built in 1979, and remains Forest Service property kept on emergency standby.

facts.design: R-6 flattop cab on 41-foot timber tower

access.note: Listed as drive-up access with emergency standby status; not offered as a public rental.

visit.trail_note: Drive-up access per Idaho Fire Lookouts; kept for emergency fire use.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Nez Perce National Forest

events.note: First Slate Point Lookout: 75-foot pole tower with 7x7-foot cab and ground cabin quarters.
Nez Perce National Forest replaced the 1931 structure with an L-4 cab on a 41-foot tower.
Current R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 41-foot timber tower replaced the 1948 L-4.
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register on April 24, 2009.
Kris Anderson staffed Slate Point, documented for seasons 2016-2019 and 2021.

evidence.supports: First lookout built 1931, pole tower, cab and ground cabin
evidence.quote: The first Slate Point Lookout was a 75' pole tower with 7'x7' cab and ground quarters built in 1931.

evidence.supports: 1948 replacement with L-4 cab on 41' tower
evidence.quote: The Nez Perce National Forest replaced it with an L-4 cab on a 41' tower in 1948
which in turn was replaced by this R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 41' timber tower in 1979
Nearby Slate Creek was named after early miners who found no placer gravel in the stream, only slate.
Slate Point Lookout has been staffed in most recent years.
Kris Anderson staffed Slate point for 5 seasons 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021 It is staffed this year, also, by regular fs hire
The present 41' treated timber tower with flat cab, built in 1979, is available during emergencies.

notes_for_editor: Build-year conflict noted in brief resolves cleanly: 1931 pole tower, 1948 L-4, 1979 current R-6 flattop, all per NHLR. Height field in brief (2.1m) likely refers to cab dimension, not tower height (41 feet); not corrected here since no source gives a clean meters figure for overall height.
